subject.title: Manual context clearing for tool results

question: Should OpenClaw add caller-directed tool-result lifecycle control, and if so should the first version be hard delete, soft archive with recovery, or only earlier automatic truncation/pruning improvements?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the API changes session persistence, replay validity, recovery semantics, and agent authority; automation should not invent that contract.

options.title: Soft Archive With Recovery
options.body: Add a core lifecycle path that removes selected tool-result content from active prompts while retaining an inspectable/recoverable transcript placeholder and recovery handle.

options.title: Hard Delete Only
options.body: Allow explicit removal of selected tool-result content from active context and transcript projection, accepting stronger risk around replay, audit, and later recovery.

options.title: No Manual Lifecycle API
options.body: Keep improving TTL pruning, overflow truncation, compaction, and plugins such as Tokenjuice without adding a new user/agent clearing contract.

recommendation.title: Soft Archive With Recovery
recommendation.body: Add a core lifecycle path that removes selected tool-result content from active prompts while retaining an inspectable/recoverable transcript placeholder and recovery handle.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest available history across session-pruning docs, release context, and adjacent context-management work.
